text:
The point is to pick the one test that would give little or no information about what the drug does to mitochondria.

A. JC-1 (5,5',6,6'-tetrachloro-…-carbocyanine iodide) accumulates in mitochondria in a potential-dependent fashion; flow cytometry of the dye therefore reports directly on mitochondrial membrane potential.  ⇒ clearly informative about mitochondrial function.

B. A luciferase/luciferin assay measures intracellular ATP.  In intact cells most ATP is produced by oxidative phosphorylation in the mitochondria; a fall or rise in total ATP after drug treatment is therefore a useful—though indirect—read-out of mitochondrial activity.  ⇒ can give mitochondrial information.

C. Mito-RTP (a rhodamine-based “MitoTracker”-type dye) specifically stains mitochondria; confocal imaging reveals their morphology, mass and, if the dye is potential-sensitive, their membrane potential.  ⇒ directly informative about mitochondria.

D. Glucose-uptake colorimetric kits measure transport of glucose into whole cells via plasma-membrane glucose transporters.  Isolated mitochondria obtained after differential centrifugation do not take up glucose (they metabolize pyruvate, fatty acids, etc.).  Performing a glucose-uptake assay on a purified mitochondrial fraction therefore tells nothing about mitochondrial activity and would be meaningless for assessing the drug’s effect on mitochondria.

Hence option D is the one experiment that will not help in discovering the mitochondrial role of the drug.

Answer: D
